title: Open a crown-capped bottle on a mounted bottle opener and serve it on a coaster
keywords: bring the workpiece to the tool
instruction: Open the bottle on the mounted bottle opener, then stand the open bottle on the coaster and let go.
context: Bartenders and servers open crown-capped bottles on counter- or wall-mounted openers many times a shift (O*NET 35-3011.00, 35-3031.00). The opener is fixed, so the bottle goes to the tool: lift it, slip the edge of the cap over the opener's tooth, and pull the bottle down so the tooth pops the cap. A crown cap can't be pulled off by hand.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); the layout is the same in every trial. (1) A green glass soda bottle, 300 g, 11.5 cm tall to the top of its neck: a 6 cm wide body 9 cm tall with a cream paper label band from 3 to 7 cm up, a shoulder 4 cm wide to 9.7 cm and 2.6 cm wide to 10.5 cm, and a neck 1.4 cm wide; standing at x 27, y -25. (2) A red steel crown cap, 2.9 cm across and 6 mm tall, 6 g, crimped on its neck. (3) A fixed bottle opener: a steel face plate 1.2 cm thick, 5 cm wide and 1.3 cm tall (13.8 to 15.1 cm above the table), its front face at x 42.5, centred on y -20, on a dark post 2 cm thick and 6 cm wide running from the table to the plate's top behind it. A flat steel tooth, 1.4 cm long, 2.4 cm wide and 3 mm thick, sticks out of the plate's front face toward the robot, its top face 14.8 cm above the table. (4) A cork coaster, 9 cm across and 4 mm thick, centred at x 31, y -4.
scoring: Judged from the video with a ruler. 0 if the bottle ever tilts more than 30 degrees or falls off the table. Otherwise: 1.0 if the cap was popped by the opener (the bottle pulled down at least 1 mm with the tooth under the cap's edge) and the bottle then stands on the coaster (axis within 3 cm of its centre, base on it, upright within 10 degrees), both grippers at least 6 cm from it and the bottle still, for 1 s; 0.75 if opened and standing on the coaster but still held or moving; 0.5 if opened; 0.25 if the cap's edge was hooked over the tooth (tooth tip 8 to 14 mm in from the cap's axis, within 1.6 cm of the tooth's centre sideways, cap underside 0 to 6 mm above the tooth) but not popped; else 0.
reset_notes: The cap is used up: crimp a new crown cap on with a bench capper (or use a new capped bottle) and stand the bottle on its mark. Throw away the popped cap.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz control). The crimp is a rule, not a deformation: the cap stays on the neck unless the opener's tooth is under its edge, and pops off with a small kick once the bottle is pulled 1 mm down under it. The neck is 14 mm wide (real: about 26 mm) so the tooth has a 6 mm catch. The cap has no skirt.
